PullRequest.Title: Minimap: keep the slider from jumping back while view zones scroll by
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #290138

### Problem

When the top of the viewport is inside a tall view zone, such as the deleted lines a chat edit shows, the minimap slider jumps back and then creeps forward while you keep scrolling down. In VS Code Insiders 1.145.0, with a 150-line-tall view zone after line 100 of a 1200-line file, the slider top went from 54px to −244px, above the top of the minimap, as soon as the zone reached the top of the viewport. It only came back into view around scrollTop 4000.

### Cause

`MinimapLayout.create` puts the slider at the first visible line plus the fraction of that line that is scrolled past. Since #111499 (53eac52308c) that fraction is `(scrollTop - offset(firstVisibleLine)) / lineHeight`, which assumes the first visible line starts at or above `scrollTop`. Inside a view zone it starts below:

```
line 100
┌─ view zone ──┐  ← scrollTop
│              │
└──────────────┘
line 101           ← first visible line, offset(101) > scrollTop

main:     partialLine = (scrollTop − offset(101)) / lineHeight              ∈ [−zoneHeight / lineHeight, 0)
this PR:  partialLine = clamp(scrollTop − offset(101), 0, lh(101)) / lh(101) = 0
```

So the slider jumps back by up to the zone's height in minimap lines, then creeps forward as the zone scrolls by. The same happens inside `editor.padding.top`. Inside a line with a taller custom line height, or in a view zone after the last line, the fraction goes above 1, so the slider runs ahead of the viewport or past the bottom of the minimap.

### Change

- Clamp `partialLine` to [0, 1] of the first visible line's own height. This adds one `getLineHeightForLineNumber` call per minimap render.
- If the first visible line is 0px tall (a custom line height can round to 0), the fraction is 0 instead of 0 / 0.
- Without view zones, padding or taller lines, the slider position is exactly as before.
- View zones are still not drawn in the minimap, and the slider height rule (#21346) is unchanged.
- `MinimapLayout` is exported and `create` takes only the option fields it reads, so the new test can call it.

### What this fixes

- The slider jumping back, often above the top of the minimap, when a view zone scrolls past the top of the viewport (#290138). It now stays on the line after the zone until the zone has scrolled by, then moves on.
- The same jump back while scrolling through the top padding.
- The slider running ahead inside lines with a taller custom line height.
- The slider overshooting the bottom of the minimap when the file ends with a tall view zone.

### What this does not fix

- #149849: with `editor.minimap.size` set to `fit` or `fill`, view zones still make the minimap and the editor drift apart.
- Inside a view zone the slider stays one minimap line tall and holds still, rather than moving through the zone proportionally.
- Dragging the slider across a tall view zone still lags behind the mouse, though less than before.
- In a simulation with view zones and `editor.scrollBeyondLastLine`, the slider still stepped back on screen twice near the end of the file, by up to 22px (59px before).

### Relation to #346387

#346387 uses the same clamp inside a larger change that maps the scroll position into a space without view zones, which also fixes #149849 and the drag lag. This PR is the minimal fix for the jump back only: +12/−3 lines in `minimap.ts` plus a test. If #346387 lands, this PR is not needed.

### How to test

The new `src/vs/editor/test/browser/view/minimapLayout.test.ts` scrolls through six layouts (no zones, one tall zone, many small zones, padding with taller lines and zones, a trailing zone, a 0px line right after a tall zone) and checks that the slider never moves back in the document, never goes above the minimap, doesn't overshoot its bottom and keeps a finite position.

```
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/view/minimapLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/view/minimapCharRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/editor/test/browser/config/editorLayoutProvider.test.ts
```

Result: 25 passing. With main's formula the new test fails: one tall zone gives a backward move and a slider top of −264px, many small zones give 98 backward moves, padding with taller lines gives 5, and the trailing zone puts the slider bottom at 622px on a 400px minimap. Without the 0px guard, the slider top in the 0px layout is NaN. `pnpm run eslint` on both files: clean.

Manually:

1. Open a file longer than the minimap, for example 1200 lines.
2. Show a tall view zone in it: let a chat edit delete about 150 lines, or add a 150-line webview editor inset from a test extension (the recording uses an inset).
3. Scroll down with the mouse wheel until the zone passes the top of the viewport.
4. Before: the slider jumps up, off the minimap, and creeps back. After: it stays on the line after the zone, then moves on.

The recording shows Insiders 1.145.0 (before, left) and this branch (after, right) side by side with the same file and scroll steps. The chart plots the slider top at each 50px scroll step.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scrolling or otherwise rendering an editor with the minimap enabled, including tall view zones, editor padding, and custom-height lines
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor render synchronously builds the minimap rendering context, queries the first visible line's vertical offset and now its height, then computes and applies the minimap slider layout. The added height query is on the render critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added lookup per editor/minimap render. The lookup binary-searches the number of custom-height line entries, so its cost is O(log H), where H is the effective number of custom-height entries; it does not iterate document lines or view zones.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread render; no queue, parallelism, or burst behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is added or bypassed. The immediately preceding vertical-offset query commits any pending line-height changes, so the added height lookup normally performs only a binary search over already-current line-height data.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call path and LineHeightsManager implementation directly establish one extra synchronous binary search per render, while also showing that the preceding offset query already performs pending-change commitment.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact nanosecond-level cost depends on the number of custom-height decorations and render frequency, but the mechanism is bounded to one allocation-free logarithmic in-memory lookup per render and is dominated by existing minimap rendering work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded CPU work but no collection-wide repetition, DOM/layout read, retained memory, or expensive boundary, and the lookup is required to correctly clamp progress for the actual first-line height.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering an editor when minimap output is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The outer Minimap view part constructs IMinimapRenderingContext before InnerMinimap.render checks RenderMinimap.None, so the new line-height lookup can execute on an editor render even though minimap drawing exits early.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one O(log H) in-memory lookup per outer minimap view-part render, with H custom-height entries; no per-line or per-zone loop is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread call with no asynchronous work or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. As in the enabled case, the existing preceding vertical-offset query has already committed pending line-height changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the code path and bounded lookup cost; lower prevalence does not affect the conclusion because the per-call mechanism is minimal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether the minimap view part is scheduled for every disabled-minimap render depends on existing view invalidation, but even when reached the added work is one bounded binary search.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the query precedes the inner disabled-minimap guard, its bounded allocation-free cost is too small to establish a concrete user-visible performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the added first-visible-line-height query through editor rendering and LineHeightsManager. Considered synchronous UI work and repeated work, including enabled and disabled minimap paths. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, serialization, cache-lifecycle, allocation, or retention mechanism was introduced, and no valid performance finding or regression-fix learning signal was established.
